speaker: Unknown
en: The top story has been that the AI models are hacked.
zh: 头条新闻是 AI 模型被黑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models went out under the internet and tested the security of several organizations.
zh: 模型上到互联网下测试了几个组织的安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it something to be scared of?
zh: 这有什么好怕的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it something to throw up your hands and worry about?
zh: 这是什么要举手投降担心的事吗？

en: No.
zh: 不。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've done all of these things before.
zh: 你以前做过所有这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have created containerization and boundaries.
zh: 我们创建了容器化和边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have secured applications with vulnerabilities.
zh: 我们保护了有漏洞的应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: The qualities of these agents, they're unpredictable.
zh: 这些智能体的特质，它们是不可预测的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're irrational.
zh: 它们是非理性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're prone to lashing out.

en: And as you go through this list, you arrive at the point where you're like, Jesus, these sound like interns.

speaker: Unknown
en: If you just start with, oh, well, it's just going to run as me, that's going to end poorly.
zh: 如果你只是从，哦，好吧，它就当作我来运行开始，那结局会很糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, you're going back to first principles, but you also have to go even a little deeper and start to redefine what does containerization even mean for you?
zh: 是的，你回到了第一性原理，但你也得甚至再深入一点，开始重新定义对你来说容器化到底意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The issue was never that the CISO didn't know it was broken.
zh: 问题从来不是 CISO 不知道它坏了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The issue and the difficult part of being a CISO was knowing what to fix.
zh: 问题是做 CISO 最难的部分是知道要修复什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you had a finite resource, which was a programmer, and now that seems that the math is gone.
zh: 因为你拥有有限的资源，那是个程序员，而现在看来那个数学已经没了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're only three weeks out from massive supply chain pain, but...
zh: 我们距离大规模供应链痛苦只有三周了，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Wait, what's the massive supply chain pain?
zh: 等等，什么大规模供应链痛苦？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 噢，伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: When OpenClaw first appeared inside Microsoft, the security team's reaction was familiar.
zh: 当 OpenClaw 首次出现在微软内部时，安全团队的反应很熟悉。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we ban this?
zh: 我们怎么禁用它？

speaker: Unknown
en: The next question turned out to be much more important.
zh: 下一个问题结果要重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we make it work?
zh: 我们怎么让它工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode from Black Hat, A16Z's Joel de la Garza sits down with Microsoft Gaming Deputy CISO Aaron Zolman to talk about securing AI agents that can access data, use tools, write code, and act on behalf of employees.
zh: 在这一集来自 Black Hat 的节目中，A16Z 的 Joel de la Garza 与微软游戏副 CISO Aaron Zolman 坐下来谈谈保护可以访问数据、使用工具、编写代码并代表员工行事的 AI 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They discuss why agents need their own identities, what air-gapped means when a model can find unexpected paths to the internet, and why securing this new generation of software requires both new controls and some very old security fundamentals.
zh: 他们讨论了为什么智能体需要自己的身份，当模型能找到通往互联网的意外路径时，气隙意味着什么，以及为什么保护这一代新软件既需要新的控制也需要一些非常旧的安全基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also explore a bigger shift happening inside security teams.
zh: 他们还探讨了安全团队内部正在发生的更大转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: As AI becomes impossible for companies to ignore, the CISO's job is increasingly not just to prevent risk, but to figure out how to safely say yes.
zh: 随着 AI 变得让公司无法忽视，CISO 的工作越来越多地不仅仅是预防风险，而是弄清楚如何安全地说是。

speaker: Unknown
en: So today we've got Aaron Zolman from Microsoft, the deputy CISO over there, responsible for a whole lot of different things.
zh: 所以今天我们邀请了微软的 Aaron Zolman，那边的副 CISO，负责一大堆不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've been at the forefront, like everyone, I guess, at this point, dealing with AI, AI rollout into an environment.
zh: 你一直处于前沿，就像每个人一样，我猜，在这一点上，处理 AI，AI 部署到环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're probably at a company that's leaning in a lot more to AI than probably most companies, and everybody's leaning in significantly.
zh: 而且你可能身处一家比大多数公司更深入 AI 的公司，而且每个人都在显著深入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you so much for joining.
zh: 所以非常感谢你的加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd love to talk, like, the last couple weeks...
zh: 我们很想聊聊，比如，过去几周……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's funny, it's like weeks have become like dog years, right?
zh: 很有趣，就像几周已经变成了像狗的年份，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like every week is seven weeks in old world time.
zh: 就像每周是旧世界时间的七周。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last couple of weeks have been very focused on the top story has been that the AI models are hacking.
zh: 过去几周非常集中在头条新闻是 AI 模型在黑客攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we saw there was a disclosure from OpenAI that they were doing a red team.
zh: 我们看到 OpenAI 有一个披露，他们在进行红队测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, it turns out now, just 15 minutes ago, there was another disclosure that these have all essentially happened because there was a red team exercise where someone was testing the models, right?
zh: 嗯，实际上，结果是现在，就在 15 分钟前，又有另一个披露，这些基本上都发生是因为有一个红队演习，有人在测试模型，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So they were saying,
zh: 所以他们在说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, Model, you're in this closed environment.
zh: 嘿，模型，你在这个封闭环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need you to go test the security of this organization.
zh: 我们需要你去测试这个组织的安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turned out that the environment wasn't closed.
zh: 结果环境不是封闭的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the models went out under the internet and tested the security of several organizations.
zh: 所以模型上到互联网下测试了几个组织的安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I guess to people who haven't been working with this stuff, it sounds very shocking.
zh: 所以我猜对于那些没有一直在用这些东西的人来说，这听起来非常令人震惊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Ben Horowitz at RSA this year...
zh: 我想 Ben Horowitz 今年在 RSA 上……

speaker: Unknown
en: gave a really great talk on some work we had done internally at A16z where we were using OpenClaw.
zh: 做了一个非常好的讲座，关于我们在 A16z 内部做的一些工作，我们在那里使用 OpenClaw。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we found that with OpenClaw, the guardrails, at least for Opus 4.6, kind of disappeared.
zh: 我们发现用 OpenClaw，护栏，至少对于 Opus 4.6，有点消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you'd be
zh: 所以你会

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a number of us got really obsessed with impossible tasks, right?
zh: 我想我们很多人真的对不可能的任务着迷了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like, hey, OpenClaw, I want you to do this thing for me, but there's no clear, legitimate path to do it, right?
zh: 于是就像，嘿，OpenClaw，我希望你为我做这件事，但没有明确的、合法的途径来做这件事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like basically saying, hey, Mike, I want you to go get me a diamond ring, but Mike has no credit card, no money, no ability to raise money.
zh: 所以这基本上就是说，嘿，Mike，我希望你去给我弄一枚钻石戒指，但 Mike 没有信用卡，没钱，也没有筹款的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what's Mike going to do if he has no more?
zh: 那么如果 Mike 没有更多资源了，他会怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: He's going to go rob.
zh: 他会去抢劫。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we noticed that these models would essentially basically do anything to achieve their objective.
zh: 于是我们注意到，这些模型本质上基本上会为了达成其目标而不择手段。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we'd say things like, hey, could you
zh: 于是我们会说诸如此类的话，嘿，你能

speaker: Unknown
en: Add a super user to this database, starting from zero.
zh: 从零开始给这个数据库添加一个超级用户吗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what did it do?
zh: 它做了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It found a SQL injection exploit.
zh: 它找到了一个 SQL 注入漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took over the SQL database and it added an admin user.
zh: 它接管了 SQL 数据库并添加了一个管理员用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it seems like this is coming more into focus now.
zh: 看来现在这一点正变得更加引人注目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know you've been very active in OpenClaw, which I think two months ago was the number one thing everyone was afraid of.
zh: 我知道你在 OpenClaw 方面一直非常活跃，我认为两个月前这还是每个人最害怕的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now no one talks about it, maybe six months ago.
zh: 现在没人谈论它了，也许是六个月前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it seems like everyone's using it.
zh: 而现在似乎每个人都在使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would love to hear maybe your experiences with that and kind of how you thought through that problem, because it's a very similar problem.
zh: 很想听听你在这方面的经历，以及你是如何思考这个问题的，因为这是一个非常相似的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think we were terrified of it at first, right?
zh: 我的意思是，我认为起初我们对此感到恐惧，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: As everyone was.
zh: 就像所有人一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: This thing explodes.
zh: 这东西爆发了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone wants to install it overnight.
zh: 每个人都想在一夜之间安装它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has no guardrails.
zh: 而且它没有护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has no guardrails.
zh: 它没有护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And worse than that, you know, it had fully open, remote, pull-whatever-down-from-the-internet-supply-chain pain.
zh: 比这更糟的是，你知道，它拥有完全开放的、远程的、从互联网拉取任意东西的供应链隐患。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our immediate reaction was, how do we ban this?
zh: 所以我们的直接反应是，我们要如何禁止它？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the immediate reaction after that was, well, wait, everyone wants to do this.
zh: 然后在那之后的直接反应是，好吧，等等，每个人都想做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we find a way to make this work?
zh: 我们要如何找到一种方法让它行得通？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the product people saw and said, actually, there's a really great product here.
zh: 然后产品人员看到了并说，实际上，这里有一个非常棒的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, absolutely, right?
zh: 是的，我的意思是，绝对是的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a really great product here.
zh: 这里有一个非常棒的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the foundations and the community and the kind of things that if we can show that we can run it safely, then it's going to be really powerful for people.
zh: 这里有基础和社区，以及各种东西，如果我们能表明我们可以安全地运行它，那么它对人们来说将非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was this big, multi-month, multidisciplinary effort that kind of kicked off.
zh: 所以这是一项庞大的、多月的、多学科的努力，算是启动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to preview the ending a little bit of it, Peter Steinberger, the founder of OpenClaw, is on stage at Microsoft Build with us a few months later talking about how we're bringing security to the process.
zh: 为了稍微预告一下它的结局，OpenClaw 的创始人 Peter Steinberger，几个月后和我们一起在 Microsoft Build 的舞台上谈论我们如何为该流程带来安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so is it something to be scared of?
zh: 那么它是值得害怕的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it something to throw up your hands and worry about?
zh: 它是需要让你举手无策并担忧的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, right?
zh: 不，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've done all of these things before.
zh: 我们以前做过所有这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have created containerization and documentaries.
zh: 我们创造了容器化和纪录片。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have...
zh: 我们有...

speaker: Unknown
en: We have secured applications with vulnerabilities.
zh: 我们通过漏洞保护了应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have created corporate environments that carry taint and data protection through a number of different applications that people want and that maybe we as security people wish they didn't.
zh: 我们创建了企业环境，这些环境在许多人们想要的不同应用程序中携带污点和数据保护，也许我们作为安全人员希望它们不要这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just that we have to do all of those things together and a lot faster.
zh: 只是我们必须把所有这些事情一起做，而且要快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yeah, I mean, I think it's been a really good story of thinking about all of those pieces in isolation.
zh: 所以，是的，我的意思是，我认为这是一个非常好的故事，可以孤立地思考所有这些部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really interesting.
zh: 真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you step up one level and you think through
zh: 如果你提升一个层级并思考

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of more abstractly, the way that these things behave.
zh: 更抽象地，这些东西的行为方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess generally people would refer to them as agents, but it's like a harness and a model and whatever, right?
zh: 我想通常人们会把它们称为智能体，但这就像是一个马具和一个模型之类的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like tomato, tomato, potato, whatever.
zh: 就像 tomato，tomato，potato，无所谓。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really interesting because as you work through the threat model, as you think about kind of like how do we secure these things and protect these things, you start to articulate the qualities of these agents and you're sort of like, well, they're unpredictable.
zh: 这真的很有趣，因为当你处理威胁模型时，当你考虑我们要如何保护这些东西和保护这些东西时，你开始阐明这些智能体的特质，你会有点像，嗯，它们是不可预测的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're irrational.
zh: 它们是非理性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're prone to lashing out if they don't get their way.
zh: 如果它们不顺心，它们很容易爆发。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you go through this list, you arrive at the point where you're like, Jesus, these sound like interns.
zh: 当你浏览这份清单时，你会到达这样一个地步，你会觉得，天哪，这些听起来像实习生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sort of like, these sound like interns maybe after they drank a little bit too much the night before and they come into the office.
zh: 有点像，这些听起来像实习生，也许是前一天晚上喝多了之后来到办公室的实习生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's funny, internally as a team, we've been joking about, I think we actually have a lot of great tools for managing the risks of things going irrationally inside of a company because we work with humans.
zh: 有趣的是，作为一个团队，我们在内部一直开玩笑，我认为我们实际上有很多很棒的工具来管理事情在公司内部变得非理性的风险，因为我们要与人打交道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm curious, it sounds to me like the more that I double click on this, it doesn't sound like magic.
zh: 所以我很好奇，这对我来说，似乎我越深入挖掘这事儿，它听起来并不像魔法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just sounds like you're going back to first principles.
zh: 这听起来你只是回到了第一性原理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basic blocking and tackling.
zh: 以及基本的阻截和擒抱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's more than that, right?
zh: 嗯，不止于此，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There is some special stuff you have to do because I think what makes these tools so powerful, right?
zh: 你必须做一些特殊的事情，因为我认为是什么让这些工具如此强大，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The story is when Microsoft Scout, which was sort of our like open call for the enterprise, was initially released to internal use.
zh: 故事是这样的，当 Microsoft Scout 发布时——这有点像是我们在企业界的公开招募——最初是供内部使用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The adoption curve was like phenomenal, right?
zh: 采用曲线是非常棒的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really fun, really validating as a security person.
zh: 作为一名安全人员，这真的很有趣，真的很让人有满足感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not even on the pilot group, right?
zh: 而且我甚至不在试点组里，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because everyone wants to use it and they all want to use it to connect everything.
zh: 这是因为每个人都想使用它，而且他们都想用它来连接一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think, you know, when you bring in an intern, your perspective is, well, I'm going to give them, like, two or three things they need to do their job.
zh: 所以我认为，你知道，当你带进一个实习生时，你的视角是，好吧，我会给他们，比如说，两三件他们工作需要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to make OpenClaw, Scout, these harnesses effective, you want to give them everything.
zh: 但是为了让 OpenClaw、Scout、这些套索有效，你想给他们一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do think, yes, you're going back to first principles, but you also have to go even a little deeper and start to redefine, like, what does containerization even mean for you?
zh: 所以我确实认为，是的，你是在回到第一性原理，但你也不得不深入一点，并开始重新定义，比如，容器化对你来说意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does air-gapped mean?
zh: 物理隔离意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does air-gapped mean?
zh: 物理隔离意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is an identity?
zh: 什么是身份？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because...
zh: 因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: If you just start with, oh, well, it's just going to run as me.
zh: 如果你只是从，哦，好吧，它就作为我来运行开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to take my token directly from my browser cache and do whatever it wants to do with that token.
zh: 它会直接从我的浏览器缓存获取我的令牌，并用那个令牌做任何它想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's going to end poorly.
zh: 那结局会很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I can give it its own identity, if I can describe the balance of the container, if I can tie the actions of the agent or the harness or the model or the session, actually quite hard to figure out what you want to tie to, but put that aside for a moment.
zh: 但是，如果我能给它它自己的身份，如果我能描述容器的配平，如果我能将智能体或套索或模型或会话的行为联系起来——其实很难弄清楚你想关联什么，但先把那个放一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can tie that to a particular set of logs, set of things, then you can get to the place where you are just doing your basic blocking and tackling, where you're thinking about, okay, what is the opportunity for an adversary to do this, even if that adversary is the model?
zh: 如果你能将其关联到一组特定的日志、一组东西，那么你就能到达那个你只是在做基本阻截和擒抱的地方，你在思考，好吧，对手做这件事的机会是什么，即使那个对手就是模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I monitor it?
zh: 我如何监控它？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I respond to it?
zh: 我如何响应它？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a weird, just with our basic playing around with Opus 4.6 in an environment that we thought was, it was a cloud container, so it had a policy of no internet access, but it still figured out how to get a tunnel out to Cloudflare, how to get around our controls, and then it started tunneling stuff through DNS.
zh: 这很奇怪，只是我们在一个我们认为安全的环境中用 Opus 4.6 进行了基本的玩耍，那是一个云容器，所以它有一个无互联网访问的策略，但它仍然设法找到了一条通往 Cloudflare 的隧道出口，如何绕过我们的控制，然后它开始通过 DNS 隧道传输东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It really reminds me of a long time ago when I was building more high-secure environments.
zh: 这真的让我想起很久以前，当我构建更高安全性环境的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would always have to go through the list threat model, which was like, there's all these things an attacker could do.
zh: 你总是要过一遍威胁模型清单，就像，有所有这些攻击者能做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you would always be like, well, there's 20 things here.
zh: 而你总是会想，好吧，这里有 20 件事。
